extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who practice before the USPTO (particularly those filing trademark documents) and USPTO enforcement/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, prohibited conduct, and remedial requirements set out in a USPTO Final Order disciplining a practitioner for misleading solicitation letters and improper direct contact with prospective trademark clients. Covers specific rule violations, imposed sanctions, compliance deadlines, and procedural enforcement steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction and applicability of Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19; practitioners who engage in practice before the Office (e.g., filing trademark registration documents) are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice before the Office includes filing documents in trademark registrations before the USPTO; being an active member of a state bar and having prior good standing does not remove USPTO jurisdiction. Citation to jurisdictional statutes and regulations is the basis for disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.701 — Communications concerning a practitioner's services (no misleading solicitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications about a practitioner's services must not be misleading; sending solicitations that are confusing or may be misconstrued as being mailed by the U.S. Government violates § 11.701.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of misleading conduct: solicitation letters mailed under the name 'Intellectual Property Services USA Incorporated' with an Alexandria, Virginia correspondence address that did not make a reasonable impression of being from a trademark practitioner and could be misunderstood as government mail. Obtaining a prior legal opinion does not excuse conduct that otherwise violates the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.703(c) — Direct contact with prospective clients (labeling solicitation envelopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making direct contact with prospective clients by mail, the outside envelope must include the words 'Advertising Material'; failing to include that label on the outside envelope violates § 11.703(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the absence of the words 'Advertising Material' on outside envelopes as a concrete violation. Solicitations that do not clearly indicate they are advertising risk being misleading and breaching direct-contact restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filings arising from prohibited solicitation operations during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the probationary period, the practitioner shall not submit any additional filings with the USPTO arising from IPS operations or that do not otherwise comply with the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative compliance requirement tied to the sanction: filings connected to the offending corporate operation are barred unless they fully comply with professional conduct rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand and probation as sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner shall be publicly reprimanded and placed on a twenty-four (24) month probationary period beginning on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Reprimand and Probation is to be published (see publication requirements). Public reprimand and probation are the specific sanctions imposed for the violations set forth (§§ 11.701 and 11.703(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to withdraw from or dissolve business entity (IPS) by deadline and provide proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall withdraw from IPS as soon as possible by merger or dissolution under Swedish law, but no later than December 31, 2015; on or before that date the practitioner must submit an affidavit/declaration attesting compliance and copies of relevant documents evidencing IPS's dissolution or merger so the practitioner has no ownership or other interest in IPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a concrete remedial step imposed to sever the practitioner's connection to the source of the misconduct. The required submissions are legal attestations plus documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED enforcement powers and Order to Show Cause procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director in good faith believes the practitioner failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend the practitioner for up to six (6) months; the Order to Show Cause is sent to the practitioner's last address of record and the practitioner has thirty (30) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after the 30-day response period the OED Director remains of the opinion there was noncompliance, the OED Director will deliver the Order to Show Cause, any response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to six months. Any review of such suspension does not stay the suspension. The OED may also pursue further discipline for the underlying misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements following discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Reprimand and Probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should describe the practitioner, the nature of the violations (§§ 11.701 and 11.703(c)), the sanction (public reprimand and twenty-four month probation), and basic factual context (e.g., that solicitations were confusing/misleading and lacked 'Advertising Material' on envelopes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters (aggravation/rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) when addressing further complaints or in any future disciplinary proceeding against the practitioner, either as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements/representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner's past disciplinary record may be used to increase future discipline or to counter representations made by or on behalf of the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating/background matters do not preclude finding a violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior good standing (e.g., active membership and good standing in the State Bar of California, no prior discipline) and obtaining a legal opinion in advance are noted factual background but do not prevent the conclusion that the conduct violated USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order lists these facts (good standing, no prior discipline, prior legal opinion) as background; they may influence sanction severity but do not excuse violations when the conduct itself breaches the rules.
